subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Video Generation
description: A fast breakdown of AI Video Generation for builders.

hook.text: Type 'a golden retriever surfing on a wave at sunset' and watch a realistic video appear in minutes.

buildup.text: Video generation extends image diffusion to temporal sequences — frames that move coherently.

discovery.text: Models like Sora generate photorealistic video clips from text prompts alone.

twist.text: Physics breaks subtly — water flows wrong, fingers bend weirdly, shadows shift impossibly.

climax.text: Each generation fixes more artifacts. Fully convincing AI video is a matter of when, not if.

punchline.text: From still images to moving stories. The pixels learned to dance.

quiz.question: What current limitation do AI video generators have?
options: They sometimes produce physically incorrect details like wrong shadows
They can only generate black and white video
They require weeks to render a single frame

details.summary: AI video generation creates realistic motion footage from text descriptions or still images. Models like Sora can produce short clips that resemble professional cinematography.
details.whyItMatters: Video generation could democratize filmmaking but also supercharge misinformation. Understanding the technology helps society prepare for both its creative promise and its risks.
takeaways: AI generates video from text prompts or reference images
Quality is approaching professional cinematography standards
The technology poses both creative opportunities and risks

faq.question: How does AI generate realistic video from text?
faq.answer: Models like Sora use diffusion techniques similar to image generation but extended to temporal sequences. They learn motion patterns from millions of video clips to produce coherent movement.

faq.question: Can AI-generated video be distinguished from real footage?
faq.answer: Current models sometimes produce tell-tale artifacts like distorted hands or inconsistent physics. However, quality is improving rapidly and reliable detection is becoming harder.
